findings.claim: Hobbes (d. 1679, PD): Leviathan (1651), en.wikisource, ch. XIII 'Of the Naturall Condition of Mankind'. Page source = Internet Archive scan 'leviathanormatte00hobb'; page does NOT name the Head edition. Reference: Part I, ch. XIII. Excerpt: 'And the life of man, solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short.' Heading: 'Warre of every one against every one.' (the phrase 'warre of every man against every man' is not verbatim; page has 'such a warre, as is of every man, against every man'). Search engine warns the transcription has formatting breaks.
Hobbes ch. XVII, same edition. Excerpt: 'And Covenants, without the Sword, are but Words, and of no strength to secure a man at all.'

Locke (d. 1704, PD): Second Treatise ch. II, wikisource page 'Two Treatises of Government/Book II/Chapter II' (cites Index:Two_Treatises_of_Government.djvu, edition year not stated on page). Reference: Second Treatise ch. II, section 6. Excerpt: 'The state of nature has a law of nature to govern it, which obliges every one'.

Locke ch. VIII and XIX: the .../Book_II/Chapter_VIII and Chapter_XIX URLs returned 404. Content opened instead from the 1764 edition page (not 1690), a single 324k-character page, chapters as anchors. Ch. VIII s.95: 'MEN being, as has been said, by nature, all free, equal, and independent, no one can be put out of'. Ch. XIX s.222: legislators acting against their trust 'put themselves into a state of war with the people'. Citation system: chapter and section number. Chapter anchors listed at the Book II page.

Rousseau (d. 1778, PD): Du contrat social. fr.wikisource chapter URLs I guessed (Du_contrat_social/Livre_I) gave 404; the Edition_1782 page only links scanned pages of the 'Collection complete des oeuvres' t1. Opened page djvu/208 (Livre I ch. I 'Sujet de ce premier Livre'): 'L'homme est né libre, & par-tout il est dans les fers.' Opened djvu/221 (ch. VI 'Du pacte social'): 'Trouver une forme d'association qui défende & protege de toute la force commune la personne & les biens de chaque'. Orthography is 18th-century (& instead of et); a modernised line should be flagged as normalised. Reference: Livre I, chap. I and VI.

Rousseau ch. VI second page opened: https://fr.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Rousseau_-_Collection_compl%C3%A8te_des_%C5%93uvres_t1.djvu/221 ; Edition_1782 index page https://fr.wikisource.org/wiki/Du_contrat_social/%C3%89dition_1782 (note: this is 1782 collected-works text, not the 1762 first edition; the 1762 Amsterdam scan exists at e-rara.ch per search, not opened).

Machiavelli (d. 1527, PD): Il Principe, it.wikisource. Cap. XVIII: 'Quanto sia laudabile in un Principe mantenere la fede, e vivere con integrità, e non con astuzia, ciascuno lo intende.' and 'Bisogna adunque essere volpe a cognoscere i lacci, e lione a sbigottire i lupi.' Cap. XV: 'mi è parso più conveniente andare dietro alla verità effettuale della cosa'. Reference: capitolo (XV, XVIII). Page does not name a source edition in what was read.
Machiavelli ch. XV page: https://it.wikisource.org/wiki/Il_Principe/Capitolo_XV (opened, verified quote above).

Mill (d. 1873, PD): On Liberty (1859), en.wikisource. Ch. 1: 'the sole end for which mankind are warranted, individually or collectively, in interfering with the liberty of action of' any member (harm principle; sentence continues, 'self-protection'). Ch. 4 opening: 'WHAT, then, is the rightful limit to the sovereignty of the individual over himself?' Reference: chapter I, IV. Edition: page does not name a printing; 1859 text assumed.
Mill ch. IV page opened.

Plato (d. 347 BC, PD): Republic in Greek, Perseus Digital Library text 1999.01.0167 (the Greek text; editor was not stated in the captured page, Burnet is the usual Perseus edition: unverified). Reference: Stephanus. 338c: 'φημὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ εἶναι τὸ δίκαιον οὐκ ἄλλο τι ἢ τὸ τοῦ κρείττονος συμφέρον.' 359c: 'δόντες ἐξουσίαν ἑκατέρῳ ποιεῖν ὅτι ἂν βούληται, τῷ τε δικαίῳ καὶ τῷ ἀδίκῳ'. 359d (Gyges): 'ποτὲ φασιν δύναμιν τῷ Γύγου τοῦ Λυδοῦ προγόνῳ γενέσθαι.' Note: pages are large (133k chars) and the passage was only reached with an offset, so a later fetch should use offset 100000. el.wikisource guess URL returned 404 (single try).
Plato 359c/359d pages: .../book%3D2%3Asection%3D359c and .../section%3D359d (same Perseus work id), opened.

Aristotle (d. 322 BC, PD): Politics, Perseus text 1999.01.0057, ed. W. D. Ross, Aristotle's Politica, Oxford 1957 (page states this; note the 1957 Ross edition itself may carry a copyright, so linking only, not copying a long text; PD status of editor's apparatus is unverified). Reference: Bekker numbers. 1253a: 'ὁ ἄνθρωπος φύσει πολιτικὸν ζῷον'. III 1279a: 'ὅσαι μὲν πολιτεῖαι τὸ κοινῇ συμφέρον σκοποῦσιν, αὗται μὲν ὀρθαὶ τυγχάνουσιν οὖσαι κατὰ τὸ ἁπλῶς δίκαιον'.
Aristotle Politics III 1279a page opened.

Wollstonecraft (d. 1797, PD): A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, en.wikisource page is a scan of a 1792 Boston printing (Peter Edes), not the London first edition. Introduction: 'My own sex, I hope, will excuse me, if I treat them like rational creatures, instead of flattering their fascinating graces.' Reference: chapter or introduction (Dedication, Introduction, Chapters I-XIII).

Marx (d. 1883) and Engels (d. 1895), PD: de.wikisource 'Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei (1848)'. Excerpts: 'Ein Gespenst geht um in Europa – das Gespenst des Kommunismus.' and, under chapter 'I. Bourgeois und Proletarier': 'Die Geschichte aller bisherigen Gesellschaft ist die Geschichte von Klassenkämpfen.' The undated base page (Manifest_der_Kommunistischen_Partei) lists multiple editions (1848 London, 1850/51 Cologne). Reference: chapter I-IV and preamble. Only the 1848 page was checked for chapter headings.

Burke (d. 1797, PD): Reflections on the Revolution in France, en.wikisource page labelled (1790); the page itself says the source document is not known. Reached text partly: 'It is a partnership in all science; a partnership in all art.' (full famous sentence about the dead, living and unborn not read, text is 584k chars, only offsets 0-300000 tried). The reflections have no chapter numbers; the reference is page of the 1790 print or the text position, needs the Dodsley page number from a scan: unverified.

More (d. 1535, PD): Utopia in Latin, la.wikisource 'Utopia' (title 'De optimo statu reipublicae deque nova insula Utopia', 1516; page names the 1518 Basel edition as source). Subpage Utopia/Liber_II/De_Utopiensium_insula (title page matched) gave: 'Harum quæ proximæ inter se sunt millia quatuor ac uiginti separant.' and 'Nulli urbi cupido promouendorum finium.' Reference: Liber II, section heading. The first Liber II fetch returned only the table of contents (no text), second try on the subpage worked.

Tocqueville (d. 1859, PD): fr.wikisource 'De la démocratie en Amérique/Édition 1848/Tome 1/Introduction'. Excerpt: 'Parmi les objets nouveaux qui, pendant mon séjour aux États-Unis, ont attiré mon attention' (continues 'aucun n'a plus vivement frappé mes regards que l'égalité des conditions'). Reference: Tome I, Introduction; Tome I, 1re partie chap. 4 on popular sovereignty also linked. The Edition 1848 base page also gives Edition 1866 as alternative.

Constant (d. 1830, PD): fr.wikisource 'Œuvres politiques (Constant)/De la liberté des Anciens comparée à celle des Modernes' (speech 1819; the page is from the 1874 Louandre collection, sourced from Gallica). Excerpts: 'La liberté individuelle, je le répète, voilà la véritable liberté moderne.' and 'Je me propose de vous soumettre quelques distinctions, encore assez neuves, entre deux genres de liberté,'. Reference: speech sections, no standard numbering. First guessed titles (two URLs) returned 404; third, from search, worked.

Kropotkin (d. 1921, PD): en.wikisource Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution (1902) is English text (page lists French and Russian editions; marked 'incomplete'). Conclusion: 'The unsociable species, on the contrary, are doomed to decay.' This is a work of biology-sociology; for anarchism proper (The Conquest of Bread, Anarchist Morality) a political text was not opened (not tried).

Snellman (d. 1881, PD): 'Läran om staten' (Stockholm: Haeggström, 1842) exists as a digitised copy at Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, DDB record states Public Domain Mark 1.0, viewer http://digital.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de/dms/werkansicht/?PPN=PPN656442476 (record read, viewer image not opened, no OCR text so no excerpt). No Litteraturbanken, Doria or Runeberg full text found in two searches. HathiTrust also lists a scan (not opened). Excerpt could not be provided.

recommendations: Take Hobbes and Locke citations from chapter and section number, not from Wikisource page names; for Locke use the 1764 page or find a 1690 scan before calling it the 1690 text.
For Rousseau note the Wikisource source is a 1780s collected edition with & for et; either link the 1762 e-rara scan (found, not opened) or label the modernised spelling.
For Plato and Aristotle link the Perseus Greek pages (Stephanus and Bekker references work); Ross 1957 is a modern critical edition, so link only and don't copy long passages.

Snellman: use the Berlin scan only as the open link; provide an own translation from a scan reading by a Swedish reader, or choose a shorter, easier source; a reviewer must check the page image because no OCR text was read.

Burke: read the 'partnership' paragraph on the page (offset beyond 300000) before choosing an excerpt; Kropotkin: pick a political text (Conquest of Bread or Anarchist Morality) and open its page; neither was opened.
WebFetch only returns short quotes (about 125 characters), so excerpts need a second pass against the page or scan before the contract fields are filled.

research.summary: Neutrality rules for FI3 (16-19-year-olds), adapted from contract §C-D and style-guide §11-12, §16. Core design: a fixed five-part "ideology card" for liberalism, conservatism, socialism, anarchism and nationalism (own words, core claims, a classic source, strongest critique, a fictional case); period-bound passages get one neutral framing sentence; the `violence` safety flag, content note and help box apply only on named triggers; no disclosure prompts; no parties, no current Finnish politicians. A checker word list is at the end. Only Aristotle was read on a page (MIT Classics). The Hobbes and Gutenberg pages failed, so the rest comes from the project's own rules plus model knowledge, graded likely or unverified.

findings.claim: Project rules already in force that FI3 inherits: contract §C (arguments with strongest critics, no advocacy, 'both sides' never makes curriculum content optional), §D (safety_flags from {death_suicide, violence}, content_note, ## Apua ja tukea, no methods, no personal-disclosure prompts); style-guide §11 table lists 'political ideas analysed by their arguments (FI3)' versus 'party names, current campaigns, advocacy'; §16 adds symmetry within a quarter in length and tone, no real group named as holding a view, checker words for disclosure prompts, and one neutral framing line for period-bound texts.

Aristotle, Politics Book I (Jowett translation, MIT Classics): parts 2, 5 and 6 treat natural slavery (some are slaves by nature, slavery by nature distinguished from slavery by law or conquest); parts 5, 12 and 13 treat the male as naturally ruling and the female as ruled, with the woman's deliberative faculty 'without authority'. Bekker numbers (about 1252a-1255b, 1259a-1260b) are from memory and unverified.

Suggested neutral framing sentence for Aristotle (Finnish, one sentence, no moral verdict and no apology): 'Aristoteles perustelee tässä kohdassa orjuutta ja naisten alisteista asemaa luonnolla; nämä käsitykset hylätään nykyisin ihmisoikeuksien vastaisina, ja tekstiä luetaan siksi argumentin ja sen virheiden tutkimisena.' Pattern: states what the author claims, states in one clause that the view is rejected today (human rights are a curriculum content item, so this is content, not opinion), and says what the student does with the text.

Locke: his Two Treatises (1689) argue against absolute monarchy and slavery as a condition, but Locke also had a role in the Carolina constitution and invested in the Royal African Company; Rousseau (Emile, book 5) assigns women a subordinate educational role. Each needs one neutral line only where the page quotes or paraphrases the relevant text; the basic facts about Locke and Rousseau are widely documented but not opened on a page in this run.

Hobbes' state of nature (Leviathan ch. 13, war of all against all, life 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short') is a thought experiment about the absence of a common power, not a description of a historical society; Hobbes' remark that 'savage people in America' resemble it is a period-bound colonial comparison and needs a one-sentence framing if quoted. Page read failed.

Rule 1, symmetry (ideology cards): each of liberalism, conservatism, socialism, anarchism and nationalism gets the same five slots (what it says in its own words and key terms; what it values most; one public-domain source, e.g. Mill, Burke, Marx and Engels, Kropotkin, Snellman; the strongest critique, formulated as the best objection its opponents make; a fictional example case). Word counts of the five cards within 25% of each other; the critique is as long as the claim section within 25%; each card's critique comes from a named rival tradition, not from the writer's voice. Order alternates between pages and is not left-right ranked in every page. Anarchism and nationalism are not demoted to a footnote or a 'dangerous ideas' tag. Written in the ideology's own terms (Finnish equivalents: vapaus, perinne, tasa-arvo, valtion vastustaminen, kansakunta), with 'sanoo' or 'perustelee' rather than 'väittää' or 'myöntää' for one side only (reporting verbs must be the same across cards).

Rule 2, no party politics: no Finnish party names or abbreviations, no named current MPs, ministers or party leaders, no current election slogans, bills or campaigns; no real contemporary group is said to hold a view; examples are historical (public-domain authors, dated events) or fictional. Historical regimes may be named only as history with a date (e.g. French Revolution, October Revolution, Finnish independence 1917) and not as support for a present-day camp. Ideologies are defined by arguments, not by who votes for them. 'Left' and 'right' appear only as defined historical terms (the 1789 seating) if at all.

Rule 3, safety_flags violence: the flag, a one-sentence content_note and a youth help box are required when a topic quotes, paraphrases or sets a task on any of: killing or execution of named people; civil war, massacre or terror as an event (French Revolution terror, 1918 Finnish civil war, Soviet purges); Marx and Engels on revolution or violent overthrow; Kropotkin or anarchist 'propaganda of the deed' and assassinations; Hobbes' war of all against all if illustrated with scenes of killing; Machiavelli on cruelty well used (Prince ch. 8, 17); nationalism and war (Snellman is mild, but 1914 or 1939 nationalism, ethnic cleansing and genocide are flagged); Thrasymachus-style 'might is right' is NOT flagged on its own. Not flagged on their own: abstract social-contract talk about 'war' as a concept, the right of resistance in Locke discussed as theory, civil disobedience, strike, protest. Rule of thumb: flag when a page names real violence, victims or perpetrators or quotes a text that approves violence; do not flag a purely conceptual mention. When in doubt, flag (cost is one sentence).

Rule 4, how violence is framed when flagged: no methods, weapons, bomb-making or attack logistics; no graphic descriptions or casualty lists; no named recent attackers or manifestos; terrorism is discussed as a political-philosophy question (how arguments for violence are justified and criticised: just war, legitimacy, proportionality, the state's monopoly on force per Weber paraphrased), with the strongest critique alongside; extremist content is never quoted beyond the minimum historical passage with a framing line. The help box: 112 first, then opiskeluterveydenhuolto, kuraattori or psykologi, then dated links (Sekasin, Mielenterveystalo nuoret, MLL Lasten ja nuorten puhelin); no MIELI Kriisipuhelin without the operator's yes. Add one study-help line for students worried about news of violence. The violence box does not duplicate the death_suicide text, and a page that touches both carries both flags. Whether Nuorten Exit (leaving violent groups) is listed for extremism needs an operator decision and its own page confirming it serves young people; the project already notes it for consent or harassment cases.

Rule 5, no disclosure prompts: no task, reflection or open question asks the student to say what they think politically, vote or would vote, what their family or religion holds, or which ideology they prefer. Tasks use: 'Erittele', 'Arvioi perustelun vahvuutta', 'Muotoile vahvin vastaväite', 'Selitä, miten X vastaisi'; a stance may be defended 'harjoituksena' with an assigned side; the teacher can assign sides by lot. A model answer accepts any argued conclusion and ends conditionally. 'Pelisäännöt' section states that reasons are judged, not people. Never a poll or 'which ideology are you?' quiz. Nothing is stored about political choices; the site has no accounts or forms.

Rule 6, symmetry and curriculum fidelity together: the curriculum content (justification of social order, rights, rule of law, democracy) is stated as content; 'both sides' framing is used only for contested questions (e.g. state versus market, tradition versus reform), never for human and civil rights or democratic rule of law as the course's frame. Slavery and colonialism are presented as past practices that thinkers justified and others attacked (Wollstonecraft, Mill on the subjection of women; Mill's own India Company career is a possible framing line, unverified), not as an open question today.

Rule 7, the teacher role: a short 'Opettajalle' box says the topic is analytical, how to hold a classroom discussion (reasons judged, assigned roles, no polling, no pressure to disclose), and how to react if a student distress or extremist statement appears (talk privately, kuraattori, no debate in front of the class). This is general practice, not copied from a source; a Finnish teacher should review it.

Utopias and dystopias (More, Utopia, in Latin) contain period-bound institutions (slavery of convicts and bondmen in Utopia; war and colonisation arguments) that need a framing line, and More's own execution in 1535 should not be told graphically.

Checker word list part 1, party and current politics (flag any hit): perussuomalaiset, kokoomus, SDP, keskusta, vihreät, vasemmistoliitto, RKP, kristillisdemokraatit, Liike Nyt, PS, KOK, KESK, VIHR, VAS, KD, eduskuntavaalit 2023, hallitusohjelma, puheenjohtaja, kansanedustaja, ministeri, pääministeri, presidentti plus any real current-politician surname (Orpo, Purra, Marin, Niinistö, Stubb, Putin, Trump, Biden, Netanjahu and the like), puolue, vaalikampanja, 'äänestä', 'äänestäisit'. Allowed with date context: historical party names only if the brief allows them (Snellman's Fennomans; SDP 1899 would need an explicit exception; default is not to name them).

Checker word list part 2, advocacy and loaded words (flag unless inside a quoted primary text with its framing line): oikea mielipide, ainoa oikea, järkevä ihminen, kaikki tietävät, selvästi, ilmeisesti väärä, vaarallinen ideologia, äärioikeisto, äärivasemmisto (only as defined historical or analytic term), fasisti, kommunisti, natsi, sosialisti, uusliberaali, woke, populisti, vasuri, kapitalisti as insult, 'pahat', 'hyvät', 'tyhmä', 'naiivi', 'huuhaa', 'hölynpöly'; asymmetric reporting verbs for one side (väittää, myöntää, muka); 'todellisuudessa', 'oikeasti' used to dismiss a position.

Checker word list part 3, disclosure prompts (extends style-guide §16): itse (when asking the student), perheessäsi, läheisesi, oma uskosi, kerro kokemuksestasi, mitä sinä ajattelet, mihin sinä uskot, mitä sinä äänestäisit, oma poliittinen kanta, kumpaa kannatat, mikä ideologia sopii sinulle, oma maailmankatsomuksesi, 'kerro ryhmälle', 'omasta mielestäsi', 'kannatatko', 'äänestätkö'. Words of the form 'mielestäsi' need a manual check (an exam-style task may ask 'perustele kantasi' only as an assigned role).

Checker word list part 4, violence and trigger terms that REQUIRE safety_flags violence, content_note and help box when present in a topic body or text box: terrori, terrorismi, terroristi, terrori-isku, salamurha, murha, murhata, teloitus, teloittaa, giljotiini, verilöyly, kansanmurha, joukkomurha, etninen puhdistus, sisällissota, vallankumous (when about the violent act or reign, not as an abstract term), vallankaappaus, vallankumouksellinen väkivalta, 'teon propaganda', pommi, räjäytys, ase, aseellinen, sota (when about real wars), sotapropaganda, internointi, vankileiri, keskitysleiri, orjakauppa, orjuus (only for the slavery pointer; usually framing line, not the violence flag), siirtomaaväkivalta. Terms that alone do NOT trigger the flag: sota as a concept in Hobbes' 'kaikkien sota kaikkia vastaan' discussed abstractly, väkivaltamonopoli (Weber), kansalaistottelemattomuus, lakko, mielenosoitus, vastarinta as a right (Locke).

Checker word list part 5, methods and glorification (hard fail, never in any topic): ohje, valmistus, resepti, ase ('how to'), pommin tekeminen, iskusuunnitelma, manifesti, kunnia (of attackers), marttyyri (of attackers), sankari (of a perpetrator of political violence), 'oikeutettu väkivalta' stated as the site's own view, names of recent attackers, graphic casualty counts from memory.

Checker word list part 6, period-bound text framing: a topic that quotes or paraphrases Aristotle (orja, luonnostaan orja, nainen, naisen alempi asema), Locke (orjuus, siirtomaat, alkuperäisasukkaat, Amerikka), Rousseau (nainen, Émile, Sophie), Hobbes (villit, Amerikka), Burke (Intia, Ranskan vallankumous), Mill (siirtomaa, barbaarit, kehityksen aste), More (orja) or Marx and Engels (Aasian tuotantotapa, sivistymättömät kansat) needs one neutral sentence within or directly after the box. Checker: if a trigger word appears in a text box and no framing line (pattern: 'Tässä kohdassa X ...; ... hylätään nykyisin ...') follows within five lines, fail.

Writer pattern for ideology cards in Finnish: heading per ideology; 'Näin se itse sanoo' (3-4 sentences in the ideology's own vocabulary), 'Tärkeimmät käsitteet' (3-5 terms), 'Lähde' (public-domain box), 'Vahvin kritiikki' (written as 'Kriitikot, esimerkiksi X-perinne, huomauttavat ...' with named tradition, not 'it is wrong'), 'Tehtävä' with a fictional case. The critique must name which of the five (or which classical author) raises it, e.g. anarchism critiqued by Hobbesian security argument, conservatism by the egalitarian objection (Wollstonecraft against Burke), liberalism by the socialist and communitarian objection (Marx; Burke on community), socialism by the knowledge and incentive objection and by the totalitarian-risk objection, nationalism by the cosmopolitan and universal-rights objection. Source attribution of the objections (Hayek, Popper, Arendt are in copyright or modern, so paraphrase and link only).

Help box wording constraint for violence-flagged topics: reuse data/yearly-facts.yaml links (Sekasin, Mielenterveystalo nuoret and similar) with dates and never type phone numbers; the existing safe-messaging rules from terveystieto apply. I did not open any of those services' pages in this run, so whether each page says it serves young people is not re-verified here.

Third-party guidance on teaching controversial and political topics (e.g. Finnish OPH's national core curriculum principle on values and Council of Europe guidance on controversial issues) was not read in this run; the rules above are therefore project-rule-based plus professional-practice reasoning and should be checked by a filosofia teacher before the judge step.

recommendations: Add an FI3 addendum to the content contract with seven rules: symmetric five-slot ideology cards (equal length within 25%, critique from a named rival tradition), no parties or current politicians, violence flag triggers (real violence named, text approving violence, terror, civil war, revolution terror, nationalism and war), help box with 112 first, no methods or glorification, no disclosure prompts, and one framing sentence per period-bound text.

Give the neutrality checker the six word lists as regex input: hard fail on parts 1 (party and current politics), 3 (disclosure) and 5 (methods and glorification); require the flag on part 4 hits; require a framing line on part 6 hits; manual review on part 2.

Have the sources checker confirm for each text where Aristotle, Locke, Rousseau, Hobbes and More were quoted that the framing line exists and says only what the author claims plus that the view is rejected today, with no editorialising.
Reread Hobbes Leviathan ch. 13 and Locke's passages on slavery and America from an opened edition (Gutenberg, Wikisource, Internet Archive) in the sources step, since this run could not open them.
Ask the operator once for a decision on MIELI Kriisipuhelin and Nuorten Exit in the violence help box; default is 112, school health services, Sekasin, Mielenterveystalo and MLL, as in FI2.
Have a filosofia teacher review the teacher box and the asymmetries in ideology cards, in particular anarchism and nationalism, before the judge accepts.

CONTRADICTION (neutrality vs primary-texts): the neutrality researcher says Hobbes could not be read, but the primary-texts researcher read Leviathan ch. XIII on en.wikisource. I re-read it: the page has 'solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short' and also the 'savage people in many places of America' remark (verified). Any FI3 topic quoting ch. XIII therefore needs the period-bound framing line for that remark, or must stop the excerpt before it.

That source is weaker than the Hobbes or Rousseau pages. Either label the quote 'Two Treatises (1764 text, Wikisource, unscanned transcription)' or find a 1690 or 1698 scan. Ch. VIII s.95 is verified on the page; ch. XIX s.222 was not re-checked by me.

Kropotkin: the primary-texts researcher opened only Mutual Aid (English, biology). I opened La Conquête du pain (2e éd., Tresse & Stock 1892, fr.wikisource), chapter 'Le Communisme anarchiste', and read two usable sentences (verified). That closes the anarchism gap.

Burke: the 'partnership ... between those who are living, those who are dead, and those who are to be born' sentence was never reached on the page. The page says its source document is unknown. The excerpt must be read before the contract, and the reference given as a 1790 Dodsley page from a scan.

Wollstonecraft (a passage other than the Introduction) and Mill's Subjection of Women, proposed for gender and equality, were not opened.

Weber is PD in the original (d. 1920; Politik als Beruf 1919), but no page was opened. Paraphrase only, as planned. Orwell (d. 1950) is PD in Finland since 1.1.2021 (likely, by the 70-year rule in data/yearly-facts.yaml), but no edition was opened. Zamyatin (d. 1937) is PD in the original. Huxley (d. 1963) is not PD.

proposal.title: Style-guide additions for FI3
proposal.detail:
1. Ideology card (T26, T27, T28). Five fixed slots per ideology:
   - 'Näin se itse sanoo' (3-4 sentences in its own vocabulary)
   - 'Tärkeimmät käsitteet' (3-5)
   - 'Lähde' (a PD box)
   - 'Vahvin kritiikki', with the critic named by tradition ('Kriitikot, esimerkiksi X-perinne, huomauttavat ...')
   - 'Tehtävä' (a fictional case)
   Rules: card lengths within 25% of each other, and the critique within 25% of the claim section. Reporting verbs are the same across cards (sanoo or perustelee; never väittää, muka or myöntää for one side only). Card order alternates between pages.
2. Ideology-comparison task type: 'Vertaa kahta yhteiskuntafilosofista teoriaa X:n kannalta' (as in YTL S24 t5, S25 t5 and K24 t5). The model answer names a second theorist, links to the tradition and a current fictional example, and accepts any argued conclusion, ending conditionally. Sides are assigned as an exercise ('puolusta harjoituksena').
3. No party politics. No Finnish party names or abbreviations, no current or recent officeholders (exam materials quote presidents, for example S25 t8 8.A; never reuse them), no campaigns or bills. Historical regimes appear with a date only.
4. Curriculum frame is not 'both sides'. Human and civil rights, democracy and the rule of law are stated as curriculum content. Symmetry applies to contested questions (state vs market, tradition vs reform).
5. Violence trigger rule: flag [violence], with content_note and help box, when a page names real violence (revolution terror, civil war, genocide, assassination) or quotes a text approving violence. Do not flag conceptual mentions (Hobbes' war as a concept, Weber's monopoly of force, civil disobedience, Locke's right of resistance as theory). No methods, no glorification, no recent attackers.
6. Period-bound framing line, one neutral sentence after any box quoting:
   - Hobbes on 'savage people in America'
   - Aristotle on natural slavery or women
   - Locke ch. IV on slavery
   - More on Utopian bondmen
   - Burke on the Revolution
   - Marx and Engels on 'civilised' peoples
   Pattern: 'Tässä kohdassa X perustelee ...; käsitys hylätään nykyisin ...'.
7. No disclosure prompts: never ask whom the student votes for, which ideology suits them, or what the family thinks. Checker word lists from the neutrality research: hard fail on party names, disclosure phrases, and methods or glorification; flag required on violence terms; manual review on loaded words.
8. 'Opettajalle' box: discussion rules, assigned roles, no polling, and how to respond privately to distress or extremist remarks. Needs teacher review (unverified practice).
